label: P2-011 named destinations A
brief: Tidewake island archipelago (pale dunes, open water): four named destinations seen from the player's stand at the same heading (a village hall, a lookout, a shrine, a cove arch). Does each named destination read as an authored place with a recognisable landmark that belongs to the world?
defects: named destination has no landmark in frame (reads as a bare slope)
landmark reads as a placeholder box or stand-in

label: P2-011 named destinations B
brief: Tidewake island archipelago: four more views of named destinations (a waterfall gate, garden terraces over the sea, a lookout from another heading, a village hall from another heading). Does each read as an authored place with a recognisable landmark that belongs to the world?
defects: named destination has no landmark in frame (reads as a bare slope)
landmark reads as a placeholder box or stand-in

label: P2-026/P2-009 water and shoals
brief: Tidewake open water seen from two shore stands: a line of small sand shoals crossing a channel, island shores and water depth. Do the water, shallows and shoals read as natural sea and sandbars that belong to the world?
defects: shoals form a ruler-straight chain of identical round discs with foam rims
white foam reads as bubble sprites
shallow halo and deep water step read as flat bands

label: F13#5 dock
brief: A Tidewake departure dock on a beach from four headings: pier, harbour props, the closed crossing barrier at the water's edge. Does the dock read as a lived-in working harbour that belongs to the world?
defects: closed-dock barrier reads as a farm fence or corral standing in the sea

label: P2-066/F13#5 currents
brief: Tidewake sea currents between islands, seen from three departure beaches and once from the water while swimming: the current lanes, their markers and how the moving water reads. Do the currents read as natural moving sea that belongs to the world, and can you tell where a current runs?
defects: current lanes read as road markings (dashed edge lines and white chevrons)
floating markers read as boxes or debris
